## K21 · K21-dma-pool — K21: dma_alloc from a fixed boot pool, or a run allocator over the free list

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Architect · Revision: 3

Evidence: Ruled (a) by the Architect (.wash/local/K21-dma-pool-ruling.md): a fixed DMA pool of 1024 pages taken from the top of RAM at boot before boot_budgets, the kernel's, DMA_OWNER's frames with a free/held bitmap, first fit linear in 1024, charging to the caller unchanged, quarantine until reboot; page lines for devices.md, budgets.md, memory.md; dma-reset-quarantine's program and case granted with their new verdicts. Forwarded to K21's implementer; checked at K21's review.

### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `0171154f73bd0a334a7c3338452484e8` · 2026-10-03T05:00:40Z

> Your predecessor's brief left dma_alloc's shape to the package or to you; the implementer brings it with a recommendation and builds the free list and the rollback meanwhile. (a) A fixed boot pool: 1024 pages (4 MiB) on both widths, taken at boot from the top of RAM beside the trace ring, marked DMA_OWNER in the table with a per-page free bitmap so is_dma_frame and every owner check keep refusing it; first fit over the pool, linear in 1024, a constant like map_anon's area; a driver asking for more than the pool's largest free run gets OutOfMemory; a quarantined run stays out of the pool for ever. Today's drivers need tens of pages per run (netd REGION_PAGES 16 slots, blkd 1+DATA_LEN, the rig's 1-page probes): 1024 is 32 runs of 32. Consequences: dma-reset-quarantine's checker, which dma_allocs every free page of root's budget, becomes a search of the pool (everything not quarantined, no overlap) - outside the brief's paths; devices.md's OutOfMemory list gains 'the pool'; boot_budgets counts root's free RAM without the pool. (b) A run allocator over the free list: a run of n contiguous frames has no bound in n or a constant without a buddy or segregated structure behind every allocation, well past size M. Implementer recommends (a) at 1024, no boot argument for the size. My view: (a); the size is yours (what MAX_RUNS and the largest driver run on the page imply), and whether the pool is charged to anyone or is the kernel's like the ring. Rule with the devices.md line and the test's new shape; grant the test file if (a).

### Architect · Answer

Event: `7ec9cf69393cc64d4f267caaa174622b` · 2026-10-03T05:04:29Z

> Ruling: (a). Full ruling and exact page lines: .wash/local/K21-dma-pool-ruling.md.
> 
> - Size: DMA_POOL_PAGES = 1024 (4 MiB), both widths, always taken, no boot argument. That is one device's MAX_RUNS runs at 32 pages each, more than three times today's largest run (9 pages: netd's ring, blkd's queue). The constant lives in one shared place (e.g. redoubt_layout). The three 32 MiB cases lose 1/8 of their RAM; the whole bench confirms them.
> - Whose: the kernel's, like the ring. One contiguous stretch from the top of RAM at boot, before boot_budgets, not in root's pages. Its frames are DMA_OWNER's for life, with a 1024-bit bitmap for free or held. So the owner checks keep refusing them, and they are never on the free list. The audits must accept a free pool frame with no run; the report names the audit that changed.
> - Charging is unchanged: a run is charged to the caller (R6). The quarantine charging stays as built. The cost: at most 1024 general frames idle.
> - First fit is linear in 1024. A request longer than the longest free stretch is OutOfMemory, with no cap per run. A quarantined run stays out of the pool until reboot.
> - Refused: (b), which has no constant bound; one region per slot, which reserves for unused slots.
> 
> Pages (exact lines in the file): devices.md (the OutOfMemory list, a pool paragraph, the quarantine residual), budgets.md (root's row and "Who pays"), memory.md ("A page's life" sentence, its diagram and caption).
> 
> Test granted: tests/programs/src/bin/dma-reset-quarantine.rs and tests/dma-reset-quarantine.toml. One search of the pool, in a budget with room for all of it. Verdicts: allocated + 2×RUN_PAGES = DMA_POOL_PAGES; no overlap with a quarantined run; the last dma_alloc(1) is OutOfMemory with budget room left. Any other case that turns red over root's RAM comes back as a message first.
